accepted.s: Who completed the construction of the Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur in 1010 CE?
accepted.x: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja I and completed in 1010 CE.
accepted.tq: Use the builder–monument association and distinguish successive Chola rulers.

accepted.s: The Brihadeeswara Temple is also known by which of the following names?
accepted.x: Brihadeeswara Temple is also called Dakshina Meru.
accepted.tq: Test the alternate-name trap by separating titles of closely related Chola temples.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brihadeeswara Temple:
1. Its vimana is about 216 feet high.
2. Its capstone is monolithic and weighs approximately 80 tonnes.
3. The entire vimana was constructed exclusively of brick and mortar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The vimana is about 216 feet high and has a monolithic capstone of approximately 80 tonnes. Statement 3 is false because only the rest of the vimana, apart from the capstone, is described as being of brick and mortar.
accepted.tq: Split the material claim from the height and weight figures to identify the overstatement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Koranganatha, an early Chola structural temple, is located at Srinivasanallur. Airavatesvara is at Darasuram and Kampaharesvara is at Tribhuvanam.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure site–temple pair and eliminate swapped locations.

accepted.s: Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was constructed during the reign of which ruler?
accepted.x: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-ruler trap to distinguish the Chola builders of major temples.

accepted.s: The stone chariot drawn by horses and the ‘Musical Steps’ are notable features of which temple?
accepted.x: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram is noted for its miniature masterpiece form, stone chariot drawn by horses and Musical Steps.
accepted.tq: Link distinctive architectural features to the correct monument rather than its builder.

accepted.s: Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I primarily to commemorate his
accepted.x: Rajendra I established Gangaikondacholapuram as a new capital to mark his Ganga expedition.
accepted.tq: Match the ruler’s achievement with the purpose behind the foundation of the capital.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram Temple?
o: It is 216 feet high and has a straight, rigid profile.
It is 216 feet high and has a circular plan.
It is 180 feet high and is entirely made of brick and mortar.
It is 180 feet high and has a concave curvilinear profile.
accepted.x: The vimana of Gangaikondacholapuram is about 180 feet high and has a curvilinear concave profile.
accepted.tq: Use the height and profile together to distinguish it from Thanjavur’s vimana.

accepted.s: In the comparison of the Chola temples at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram, the latter’s vimana is traditionally described as having a more
accepted.x: The concave curvilinear profile of Gangaikondacholapuram is described as having feminine grace, in contrast to the masculine bulk of Thanjavur.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap involving the masculine and feminine descriptions.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gangaikondacholapuram — Bronze well and giant Nandi
Airavatesvara — Stone chariot and Musical Steps
accepted.x: Brihadeeswara has a vimana of about 216 feet. The approximately 180-foot vimana belongs to Gangaikondacholapuram.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed numerical comparison among otherwise familiar temple features.

accepted.s: Kampaharesvara Temple, a late Chola monument, is situated at
accepted.x: Kampaharesvara Temple was built by Kulottunga III at Tribhuvanam and is regarded as a late Chola monument.
accepted.tq: Use the site–builder pair to distinguish the later Chola temple from earlier examples.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of the sequence given:
A. Brihadeeswara Temple
B. Shore Temple
C. Gangaikondacholapuram Temple
D. Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram
accepted.x: The sequence is Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram, Shore Temple, Brihadeeswara, and Gangaikondacholapuram.
accepted.tq: Fix the Pallava pair first, then place the two later Chola monuments.

accepted.s: Which of the following temples is an early Chola structural temple located at Srinivasanallur?
accepted.x: Koranganatha Temple at Srinivasanallur is identified as an early Chola structural temple.
accepted.tq: Combine the architectural classification with the site instead of relying on the temple name alone.

accepted.s: The Chit Sabha, containing carvings of 108 classical dance poses, is associated with the
accepted.x: The Chit Sabha of the Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram contains carvings of 108 classical dance poses.
accepted.tq: Identify the shrine through its distinctive dance-related architectural feature.

accepted.s: The Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram is dedicated to Shiva in the form of
accepted.x: The Chidambaram shrine is dedicated to Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance.
accepted.tq: Use the temple’s presiding form of Shiva to distinguish it from other Chola sculptural themes.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the great Nandi at Thanjavur is correct?
o: It is the original monolithic capstone of the vimana.
It was constructed by Rajendra I to mark the Ganga expedition.
It was added later by the Nayakas.
It was installed by Kulottunga III at Tribhuvanam.
accepted.x: The great Nandi at Thanjavur was added at a later stage by the Nayakas.
accepted.tq: Watch for the chronology trap separating the original Chola construction from later additions.

accepted.s:
Which of the following constitutes the UNESCO group known as the ‘Great Living Chola Temples’?
1. Thanjavur
2. Gangaikondacholapuram
3. Darasuram
4. Chidambaram
accepted.x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram. Chidambaram is not included in this group.
accepted.tq: Use the exclusion statement to separate a major Chola shrine from the UNESCO group.

accepted.s: The lost-wax technique perfected by the Cholas for making bronze icons is known as
accepted.x: The Cholas perfected the cire perdue, or lost-wax, casting technique for bronze icons.
accepted.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than a general description of metal casting.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the religious status of Chola bronze images?
o: They were made exclusively as architectural decorations.
They were worshipped icons noted for fine craftsmanship and expressive faces.
They were undecorated images intended for military standards.
They were used only as royal commemorative statues.
accepted.x: Chola bronzes were worshipped icons, distinguished by fine craftsmanship, intricate jewellery and expressive faces.
accepted.tq: Apply the description to distinguish ritual icons from merely decorative or commemorative sculpture.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: In the standard iconography of Chola Nataraja bronzes, the upper right hand holds the
accepted.x: The upper right hand of Nataraja holds the damaru, or drum, symbolising creation.
accepted.tq: Map each hand to its object before considering the associated philosophical meaning.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The agni held in the upper left hand of Nataraja symbolises
accepted.x: The fire, or agni, in Nataraja’s upper left hand represents destruction.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the paired meanings of the drum and fire.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The lower right hand of the Nataraja image is generally shown in the abhaya mudra, signifying
accepted.x: The abhaya mudra means ‘fear not’ and signifies protection or reassurance.
accepted.tq: Match the gesture with its meaning while avoiding confusion with the foot symbolism.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The lower left hand of Nataraja points towards the raised left foot, which signifies
accepted.x: The lower left hand directs attention to the raised foot, symbolising liberation or refuge.
accepted.tq: Use the hand–foot relationship to identify the meaning of the gesture.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: In the Nataraja icon, the right foot placed on the dwarf Apasmara represents the
o: fusion of male and female principles
accepted.x: Apasmara represents ignorance, and Nataraja’s right foot placed upon him signifies its conquest.
accepted.tq: Identify the symbolic meaning by linking the named figure Apasmara with ignorance.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the earrings of the Chola Nataraja image:
1. The right ear bears a man’s earring.
2. The left ear bears a woman’s earring.
3. They symbolise the fusion of male and female principles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The different earrings represent the fusion of male and female principles in the Nataraja image.
accepted.tq: Check the paired left–right details first, then connect them to the symbolic interpretation.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The ring of flames surrounding the dancing Nataraja is called the
accepted.x: The ring of flames is called the prabhamandala and represents the cosmic cycle.
accepted.tq: Separate names of architectural spaces, hand gestures and iconographic elements.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a Nataraja element with its meaning?
o: Right foot on Apasmara — conquest of ignorance
accepted.x: The right foot placed on Apasmara symbolises the conquest of ignorance. The upper right hand with the drum signifies creation, the upper left hand with fire signifies destruction, and the prabhamandala represents the cosmic cycle.
accepted.tq: Eliminate reversed symbolic meanings and retain the correctly matched iconographic detail.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the number of arms in the standard dancing Shiva image of Nataraja is correct?
o: It is shown with two arms.
It is shown with three arms.
It is shown with four arms.
It is shown with eight arms.
accepted.x: The standard Nataraja image represents dancing Shiva with four arms.
accepted.tq: Test the fixed numerical feature directly while separating it from other multi-armed forms.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram are particularly noted for their
accepted.x: The Dakshinamurthy panels at these two temples are regarded as among the finest examples of deep-relief stone sculpture in South India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the medium and sculptural method from the bronze tradition of the Cholas.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram are regarded as among the finest examples of this form in
accepted.x: These panels are rated among the finest deep-relief stone sculptures in South India.
accepted.tq: Use the regional comparison carefully; the geographical qualifier is the key detail.
accepted.sec: Chola bronzes - casting technique, Nataraja iconography, other forms  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nataraja image are correct?
1. The damaru in the upper right hand symbolises creation.
2. The agni in the upper left hand symbolises destruction.
3. The prabhamandala symbolises the cosmic cycle.
4. Apasmara symbolises liberation.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Apasmara represents ignorance; the right foot placed upon it symbolises the conquest of ignorance.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed meaning among several correctly paired symbols.
